heading: Child latents absorb parent features; changing SAE size or sparsity does not stop this
definition: splitting of hierarchical features is not clean; a parent latent fails to fire where a more specific child latent takes over, and changing SAE size or sparsity doesn't fix it.
summary: Several independent groups find absorption (a parent latent staying silent where a more specific child latent fires) in standard SAEs, both in toy models and in GPT-2, Pythia-70M, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B and Qwen3-4B; on Gemma-2-2B it grows with SAE width. Less sparse SAEs show less measured absorption, but no study reports it gone, and other training objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs reduce it.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: R2. Absorption in standard SAEs is reproduced by arXiv:2506.03093, which has no shared-author flag, and backed by theory. lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN shows it too, but its authors are not in the checked author list and its toy setups match the original's own toy rows (arXiv:2409.14507 r1-r4), so it is not counted as independent; arXiv:2503.17547 and arXiv:2505.11756 show it too but share authors with an original, so they count as R1 evidence. <1B: R2 for presence at a fixed width (GPT-2 small, Pythia-70M in arXiv:2606.06333 and arXiv:2510.00404; counts studies_by_size.<1B = 2); the size and sparsity clauses are not tested there. 1-10B: R2 for presence (Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen3-4B, from studies with no shared-author flag; counts studies_by_size.1-10B = 12, flagged studies included); Gemma-2-9B presence comes only from arXiv:2503.09532, which shares authors with the original, so R1 there. 'Enlarging width doesn't fix it': R2 on Gemma-2-2B (arXiv:2602.11881; arXiv:2506.01197, figure only; both with no shared-author flag), R1 on Gemma-2-9B (arXiv:2503.09532 R5 only). The sparsity clause is limited but not contested: higher L0 reduces measured absorption, and no study reports elimination. For standard SAEs on real models, the only stated result besides the original's own text is arXiv:2503.09532 R3 (R1), a direction given in the text with no values. Studies with no shared-author flag that vary L0 within one method either use other SAEs, arXiv:2604.06495 (Matryoshka, text only) and lw:rE43EfHigXcjTmomJ (MP-SAEs on Gemma-2-2b at L0≈85 and ≈265, absorption at both, figure only; its BatchTopK comparators give no readable values), or show the sweep only in a figure, with no values in these records: arXiv:2509.22033 plots BatchTopK and ReLU absorption across L0 25 to 130 (Fig 4b, figure only, not in V4 rows), and arXiv:2606.30609's sparsity sweep is only plotted (Figure 3; SAE type not stated in these records). The toy lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN r5, r6 and the original's text give the same direction (sparser means more absorption). No unconfounded absorption result points the other way: arXiv:2510.08855's dense SAEs, where the highest L0 has the highest absorption, vary method and L0 together, and arXiv:2602.11881's falling P(parent|child) across L0 is cross-size co-activation of post-hoc pairs, not absorption (V4.conflicts[0]). 10-100B and >100B: no tests (absent from counts studies_by_size).
suggested_status.reason: Baseline: the original (arXiv:2409.14507) shows absorption on Gemma-2-2B Gemma Scope SAEs and on Llama 3.2 1B, and reports higher rates in wider and sparser SAEs. Counts: versions.V4.verdicts.supports.studies = 23, limits_scope.studies = 15, challenges.studies = 0; tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 4 of studies_tested = 27. The studies index marks these four SAME GROUP: arXiv:2503.09532, arXiv:2503.17547, arXiv:2505.11756 and lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN. By the checked author lists, arXiv:2503.09532 and arXiv:2505.11756 share authors with V4's original, arXiv:2409.14507; arXiv:2503.17547 and lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN share authors with another original of this phenomenon, arXiv:2502.04878, and not with arXiv:2409.14507. All four count as R1 evidence here, never as independent. Several studies with no shared-author flag find absorption in standard SAEs on other families: Llama-3-8B and Gemma-2-2B (arXiv:2509.22033, arXiv:2606.30609, the latter with 5-seed CIs); GPT-2 and Mistral-7B (arXiv:2606.06333); Pythia-70M and Qwen3-4B (arXiv:2510.00404). Absorption grows with width on Gemma-2-2B in arXiv:2602.11881 and arXiv:2506.01197 (figure only), neither with a shared-author flag. From studies that share authors with an original, it also grows on Gemma-2-2B and Gemma-2-9B (arXiv:2503.09532) and on Gemma-2-2B layer 8 (lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN). Limits: higher L0 reduces measured absorption (arXiv:2503.09532 R3, arXiv:2604.06495); changed objectives cut it sharply (arXiv:2503.17547: 0.05 vs 0.49); Qwen3-8B shows 0.0074 (arXiv:2606.30609). Causal ablation evidence comes only from the original (counts coverage_by_operation.removal.studies = 1).
suggested_status.open_questions: Would a sparsity setting under the standard objective eliminate absorption, rather than reduce it? A stated result (in text or with readable values) from an L0 sweep on standard SAEs by a group with no shared author would give the sparsity result an independent reproduction. Besides the original's own text, the only real-model standard-SAE L0 result stated in these records (arXiv:2503.09532 R3, a direction in the text with no values) shares authors with the original. arXiv:2509.22033 plots BatchTopK and ReLU absorption across L0 25 to 130 (Fig 4b) and arXiv:2606.30609 plots a sparsity sweep (Figure 3), but neither gives values in these records; arXiv:2604.06495 sweeps Matryoshka SAEs only. Would an independent width sweep on Gemma-2-9B or another family reproduce arXiv:2503.09532 R5? Does absorption persist above 10B and in instruction-tuned models? Would an independent group's latent ablation reproduce the original's causal evidence? Does absorption hold on non-first-letter hierarchies with systematic metrics? Why is Qwen3-8B near zero? Does the diffuse-regime absence (arXiv:2609.10299) apply to real SAEs? For Iris: should a study that shares authors only with arXiv:2502.04878 (arXiv:2503.17547, lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN) count as independent for V4? No clause's level changes either way, because studies with no shared-author flag cover the same toy and Gemma-2-2B width results. A credible failed replication on standard SAEs would move the level toward C.

source.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: David Chanin; James Wilken-Smith; Tomás Dulka; Hardik Bhatnagar; Satvik Golechha; J. Bloom

original_result.setup: They trained SAEs on toy hierarchical features and measured first-letter absorption in Gemma Scope SAEs on Gemma-2-2B and in SAEs on Llama 3.2 1B and Qwen2 0.5B.
original_result.result: In toy models the child latent absorbed the parent direction and the parent latent went silent when the child fired, even in a TopK SAE with no L1 loss. In a Gemma Scope SAE the 'starts with S' latent (cosine 0.52 with a first-letter probe) did not fire on the token '_short', where ablations showed that a latent tied to that token (probe cosine 0.12) carried the first-letter information; the paper also states that absorption is higher in wider and sparser SAEs.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Theory shows absorption is possible: a child gets its own latent; the parent latent ignores it.
Absorption stayed at 0.20–0.53 across TopK, JumpReLU and AbsTopK SAEs on four models.
Absorption in standard TopK SAEs on Gemma 2-2B grew with dictionary width.
Standard SAEs on a synthetic hierarchy underestimated parent activations when children fired.
Standard SAEs had parent latents (e.g. "female") that failed to fire on child cases like "Lily".
A full-width toy SAE learned a parent encoder that excluded the child feature.
Absorption in non-Matryoshka Gemma-2 SAEs worsened as dictionary size grew.
A TopK SAE on Gemma-2-2B scored 0.14 absorption overall and 0.34 on words starting with "e".
Standard ReLU and BatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B showed substantial absorption.
Without the study's masking, Matryoshka SAEs still showed absorption at low ℓ0 on Pythia and Gemma.
Theory finds parent-child pairs unstable unless their directions match exactly; absorption into the child stabilises them.
A TopK SAE on a 1.3B GPT scored a high absorption of 0.807.
Unregularized TopK-family SAEs on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B showed absorption of 0.14–0.27.
Conventional BatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B showed about 42% absorption without the study's realignment method.
Standard SAEs on GPT-2 and Mistral-7B showed substantial first-letter absorption.
Narrow toy SAE latents mixed parent and child features, even with one latent.
BatchTopK SAE absorption rose to about 0.29 as width grew to 36864 latents.
Vanilla SAE parents skipped child tokens, and wider SAEs lost the broad feature.
In toy SAEs, the parent latent went silent where the child fired.
Toy analysis: absorption lowers sparsity loss and leaves reconstruction unchanged, so the SAE objective favours it.
Matching Pursuit SAEs on Gemma-2-2b scored worse than BatchTopK on absorption at both sparsity levels (L0).
Theory says optimal dictionary-learning solutions turn feature hierarchies into features that never fire together.
Baseline JumpReLU absorption on Gemma 2 2B rose from 0.012 to 0.156 with width.
A hierarchical SAE (H-SAE) reduced absorption and slowed its growth with width, without removing it.
Matching-pursuit SAEs (MP-SAE) showed no absorption on a synthetic hierarchy; Matryoshka SAEs sometimes avoided it.
Matryoshka SAEs removed absorption or cut it to 0.05 across toy, TinyStories and Gemma.
Toy SAEs too narrow for a child latent showed hedging (child mixed into parent), not absorption.
More active latents (higher L0) and the Matryoshka objective both reduced absorption in Gemma-2-2B SAEs.
Very dense, briefly trained SAEs showed only 0.7–1.6% absorption, far below TopK.
Raising ℓ0 (active latents) from 20 to 160 largely reduced measured absorption in Matryoshka SAEs.
In a diffuse regime with poorly aligned atoms, no absorption-type merges appeared.
In one GraphCast Matryoshka SAE pair, the parent co-fired at 95% of child sites.
A Matryoshka SAE cut absorption to 0.180, versus 0.807 for TopK.
A Batch TopK SAE on Qwen3-8B showed near-zero absorption of 0.0074.
Versus standard SAEs, the group-sparse SASA architecture cut absorption sharply in GPT-2 and less in Mistral.
A wider toy SAE with tied encoder-decoder weights learned clean parent and child latents despite co-occurrence.
Matryoshka SAEs kept absorption near 0.03 across sizes.
Toy SAE absorption was partial under some settings and vanished with tied weights.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

wording_issues.phrase: changing SAE size ... doesn't fix it
wording_issues.issue: Enlarging width raises absorption in standard SAEs (arXiv:2503.09532 R1, R4, R5; arXiv:2602.11881; lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN r2). But a toy SAE too narrow for the child shows no absorption (hedging instead, arXiv:2505.11756 R1). In lw:XHpta8X85TzugNNn2's tied toys, 5 latents for 20 features give broken latents that mix parent and children (R6, R8). 8 latents for 4 features give clean parent and child latents (R3). The post's takeaway is that tied SAEs fail when there are fewer latents than true features. Its broken cases are mixed latents, not a parent firing hole. So the clause fits enlarging untied SAEs, not every size change.

Higher L0 reduces measured absorption in arXiv:2503.09532 R3 (Gemma-2-2B, 65k, layer 12). In arXiv:2604.06495, Mean Full Absorption scores go from 86.1 to 97.4 (Pythia) and from 90.8 to 99.2 (Gemma) as ℓ0 goes from 20 to 160. arXiv:2510.08855 does not isolate L0. On Gemma-2-2B layer 12 (n=16384, 5M tokens), its dense SAEs score 0.0068 (ATM, L0 3280), 0.0114 (JumpReLU, L0 2666) and 0.0161 (standard L1, L0 8724), vs 0.1402 for TopK (L0 40). Method and L0 vary together and there is no within-method sweep. Among the dense SAEs, the highest L0 has the highest absorption. No study reports elimination. arXiv:2602.11881 (Gemma 2 2B layer 13) gives P(parent|child) of 0.662, 0.634 and 0.619 at L0 50, 80 and 100. That is cross-size co-activation of post-hoc pairs in independently trained adjacent-size SAEs, not absorption. Its SAEBench absorption is reported only at L0 about 50. The clause holds or fails depending on whether 'fix' means reduce or eliminate.

wording_issues.phrase: a parent latent fails to fire where a more specific child latent takes over
wording_issues.issue: Several results show partial absorption, where the parent fires weakly rather than not at all. lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN r4: the parent fires at 0.20. arXiv:2503.09532 (appendix text, no numbers, no row): manual inspection found absorption often partial. The absorbed latent 'still activates weakly', and several absorbing latents often share the compensation. Its metric scores absorption as a fraction for this reason. The original's baseline shows the same (arXiv:2409.14507 r3, r4). Narrow toy SAEs (fewer latents than features), tied or untied, mix parent and children instead of leaving a firing hole. lw:XHpta8X85TzugNNn2 R8: a tied 5-latent SAE merges features 5, 6 and 7 into 2 combo latents. R12 and R13: 1-latent untied and tied SAEs merge parent 0 with children 1 and 2, which the authors say is not technically absorption. Most real-model evidence is still an aggregate first-letter probe score, not observed parent firing (untested-parts lines of arXiv:2503.09532, arXiv:2607.20652 and arXiv:2609.36294).

wording_issues.phrase: splitting of hierarchical features is not clean
wording_issues.issue: Most rows measure absorption at one dictionary size, with no splitting measure. Verdict fixes drop splitting-version links because these rows measure absorption, not splitting (arXiv:2503.09532 R1, arXiv:2606.06333 R24, lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN r1). arXiv:2606.06333 calls absorption closely linked to splitting, but R24 measures absorption only. arXiv:2503.17547 is the exception. R7's fix drops only V1, because a single-size absorption rate does not show splitting as size grows, so R7 stays linked to V2, V4 and V6. That study also measures splitting separately, as latents per first letter: three for BatchTopK and one on average for Matryoshka (R9, R10; Gemma-2-2B layer 12, 65536 latents, L0=40). Outside that study, the rows assume the tie between absorption and splitting rather than show it.

Real-LLM absorption evidence mostly uses the first-letter spelling hierarchy (the SAEBench record says 'Only the first-letter hierarchy is used'; arXiv:2510.08855 adds e-words). arXiv:2602.11881's absorption evidence is also SAEBench Absorption (Gemma 2 2B layer 13, Table 1). Its T3 parent-child pairs measure nesting across dictionary sizes, not absorption. The baseline pairs are assigned post hoc by similarity, and only HSAE learns them. There are two exceptions to first-letter hierarchies. One is TinyStories female/Lily tokens (arXiv:2503.17547 R5). The other is one GraphCast pair in a Matryoshka SAE (arXiv:2610.07583 r1), where absorption is absent: parent 99 fires at about 95% of child 3153's sites (c=0.953, 95% CI [0.949, 0.956], n=15,203), and the authors say the child does not take over for the parent.

The statement names only size and sparsity, but the largest reported effects come from changing the objective or encoder. Examples: Matryoshka at 0.05 vs BatchTopK at 0.49 (arXiv:2503.17547 R7/R8); MP-SAE and tied weights removing toy absorption (arXiv:2506.03093 r4; lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN r7); SASA at 0.046 vs TopK at 0.114 (arXiv:2606.06333 R37). Read as 'absorption is inherent to SAEs', the version overreaches.

method_sensitivity.what: Absorption shifts strongly with architecture in some studies and little in others. GPT-2 layer 7 under matched training: JumpReLU 0.553, ReLU 0.267, Gated 0.240, TopK 0.114, TopK-SASA 0.046 (arXiv:2606.06333). L0=70, layer 20: ReLU 0.371 vs BatchTopK 0.220 on Gemma-2-2B, and 0.490 vs 0.148 on Llama-3-8B (arXiv:2509.22033). At a fixed 65k width, the SAEBench record ranks Matryoshka best and ReLU worst (not in rows). In arXiv:2510.00404, TopK, JumpReLU and AbsTopK differ by at most ~0.07.

Several studies report less absorption at higher L0: arXiv:2503.09532 R3; arXiv:2604.06495 with ℓ0 from 20 to 160; arXiv:2510.08855 with dense SAEs, confounded with method. The original reports higher rates in sparser Gemma Scope SAEs. In toys, raising L1 from 5e-3 to 2e-2 moves from partial to full absorption (lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN r5, r6). arXiv:2602.11881's baseline P(parent|child) falls from 0.662 to 0.619 from L0 50 to 100, but that is cross-size co-activation of post-hoc pairs, not absorption, and its SAEBench absorption is reported only at L0 about 50. No unconfounded absorption result goes against this direction, and no study reports elimination.

In standard SAEs, absorption rises with width. arXiv:2602.11881 (baseline JumpReLU, Gemma 2 2B layer 13, L0 about 50; absorption fraction reported as 1 − SAEBench score): 0.012 at 2048 latents, a low, partial level, rising to 0.156 at 16384. lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN: BatchTopK on Gemma-2-2B layer 8 rises to ~0.29 at 36864 latents (r2). arXiv:2503.09532: the Gemma Scope series worsens from 16k to 1M on Gemma-2-2B (R4) and Gemma-2-9B (R5); its own non-Matryoshka suite worsens from 4k to 65k (R1). arXiv:2506.01197: standard TopK on Gemma 2-2B layer 20 rises from 8k to 32k (figure only). Under Matryoshka the width dependence is flat or minor (lw:rKM9b6B2LqwSB5ToN r1, arXiv:2503.09532 R2).

method_sensitivity.factor: Toy setup (co-occurrence, magnitude variance, latents per true feature)
method_sensitivity.what: lw:kcg58WhRxFA9hv9vN: perfect parent-child co-occurrence gives full absorption (r2). With parent magnitude variance (sd 0.1), the parent latent fires weakly (0.20) when both are active (r4). At 95% co-occurrence the L1 coefficient decides: at 5e-3 the parent fires with reduced magnitude (r5); at 2e-2 it fails to fire when both are active (r6). arXiv:2506.03093: Vanilla and BatchTopK absorb at every within-level correlation tested (0 and 0.3 in r1, r5; up to 0.9 in text). This correlation is similarity of same-level feature directions, not firing co-occurrence; it changes recovery of within-level structure. That perfectly correlated firing favours absorption is the authors' argument (B.1.4). lw:XHpta8X85TzugNNn2: tied SAEs with 8 latents for 4 features are clean (R3); with 5 latents for 20 features, parent and children merge into broken latents, both orthogonal (R6, R8) and superposed (R10, noisier). The authors say these are not strictly absorption.

Absorption differs across models within a study. Batch TopK at L0=100 (fraction): Qwen3-8B layer 20 0.0074, Gemma-2-2B layer 12 0.1908, Llama-3-8B layer 20 0.1470 (arXiv:2606.30609). AbsTopK raw absorption per the verdict fixes: ≈0.46/≈0.47 on Pythia-70M layers 3/4, ≈0.27/≈0.30 on Gemma2-2B layers 12/14 (setup lists 16), ≈0.21/≈0.20 on Qwen3-4B layers 18/20 (arXiv:2510.00404). Baseline P(parent active | child active), for post-hoc pairs across adjacent-size SAEs and not an absorption score: 0.729 at Gemma 2 2B layer 20 vs 0.309 at Qwen3-4B layer 18 (arXiv:2602.11881). arXiv:2606.06333 standard SAEs (percent): GPT-2 layer 7 mean 37.2%, full 49.6% (ℓ0 60, 300M tokens); Mistral-7B layer 8 mean 24.0%, full 23.3% (ℓ0 285, 1B tokens). Both are externally trained SAEs of unstated type, so the model difference is confounded with the SAE.

Mean and full absorption can rank differently. GPT-2: mean 37.2% vs full 49.6%; Mistral-7B: mean 24.0% vs full 23.3% (arXiv:2606.06333, percent). arXiv:2609.36294 reports a 42.08% absorption fraction vs 38.92% full absorption. The original calls its metric conservative because it needs one dominant absorbing latent and a fully inactive main latent; its mean-logit and max-logit versions are nearly identical (not in rows). arXiv:2609.10299 uses a geometric decoder-merge criterion instead of firing. Some studies report 1 − score (arXiv:2510.00404, arXiv:2602.11881).

On Gemma-2-2B layer 12 at L0=100, C2R gives absorption of 0.1926 at λ=0.1 and 0.1726 at λ=0.5, vs a 0.1985 baseline (fraction). The main C2R setting gives 0.0656 ± 0.0185 vs 0.1908 (arXiv:2606.30609). Weighted Matryoshka does worse on absorption than equal weighting (arXiv:2503.17547). Balance-Matryoshka β moves the toy from absorption (β=0) to hedging (β=∞) (arXiv:2505.11756, text). In arXiv:2604.06495, masking probability changes the absorption scores along with explained variance.

Batch TopK absorption on Gemma-2-2B layer 12 is 0.1908 ± 0.0240 (95% CI) over 5 seeds (arXiv:2606.30609). Matryoshka's mitigation of toy absorption is inconsistent across runs (arXiv:2506.03093 r7). Toy feature matching holds on most, but not all, runs (lw:zbebxYCqsryPALh8C).

status_amendment.public_note: The summary now counts studies that share authors with the original papers as extensions of that work, not as independent reproductions, and no longer calls the sparsity result contested. It also notes that other groups' sparsity sweeps either use other kinds of autoencoder or are shown only in figures (one of them on standard sparse autoencoders), so the sparsity result for standard autoencoders on real models still rests on work by the original authors' group; the reproducibility level is unchanged.
